scenario: Customer evidence is sparse and conflicts with analytics of unknown provenance.

response.answer: Product problem: customer evidence conflicts with analytics whose provenance is unknown, so neither source can support a reliable product conclusion. Desired outcome: establish traceable, comparable evidence and resolve the contradiction. Priority: first verify the analytics’ provenance, definitions, collection method, population, and time window; then assess whether the customer evidence and analytics measure the same outcome. Exclusions: no product decision, prioritization score, value claim, technical solution, implementation, activation, or integration. Learning need: determine whether the conflict reflects sampling differences, measurement mismatch, data-quality failure, or genuinely divergent customer behavior. Recommendation: fail closed on substantive conclusions until provenance and missing decision context are supplied. Preserve any binding obligations and closed scope, neither of which is identified here.
selected_principles: PL-P04 — Preserve evidence provenance and label assumptions, unknowns, and contradictions.
PL-P05 — Do not infer authority from evidence or recommendations.
PL-P08 — Avoid unsupported numeric confidence or forecasts.
rejected_frameworks: PL-FW-PROBLEM-OUTCOME — no value definition or outcome review is specified.
PL-FW-STRATEGIC-CHOICES — no strategy formulation or competing initiatives are presented.
PL-FW-OPPORTUNITY-MAPPING — evidence is too weak and contradictory to map responsibly.
PL-FW-JOBS-CONTEXT — no user-motivation or alternative-behavior question is supplied.
PL-FW-PRIORITIZATION-ORDER — no portfolio or roadmap ordering is requested.
PL-FW-LEARNING-LOOP — no executed experiment or post-release result exists.
evidence_and_uncertainty: Evidence: customer evidence exists but is described only as sparse; its provenance and content are not provided.
Evidence: analytics conflict with the customer evidence; analytics provenance is explicitly unknown.
Unknown: product decision scope, authority state, binding obligations, task state, metric definitions, populations, time windows, and collection methods are absent.
No source is treated as more reliable, and no value, impact, causality, or confidence claim is supported.
response.authority_boundary: The candidate package has authority effect NONE, is disabled, and authorizes neither implementation nor product decisions. This classification is advisory criterion application only and causes no activation or integration effect.
